questions.questionEn: A 2-year-old child presents with audible stridor, drooling, and extreme agitation. The child is leaning forward with their mouth open. Which action is the most appropriate next step in management?
questions.questionZh: 一名 2 岁儿童出现可闻及的 stridor（喘鸣）、流涎，并极度烦躁不安，正身体前倾、张口呼吸。下一步最恰当的处理是什么？

options.en: Perform vigorous oropharyngeal suctioning of secretions
options.zh: 对口咽部分泌物进行剧烈吸引

options.en: Force the child to lie supine for a detailed auscultation
options.zh: 强行让患儿仰卧，以便进行详细的肺部听诊

options.en: Allow the child to remain in their position of comfort
options.zh: 让患儿保持其自己选择的舒适体位

options.en: Immediately insert an oropharyngeal airway to maintain patency
options.zh: 立即置入口咽通气道（OPA）以维持气道通畅

questions.explanationEn: Stridor, drooling and a tripod posture in a toddler point to a severe supraglottic obstruction such as epiglottitis. The swollen tissue is held open only by the child's own posture and calm respiratory effort, so the priority is to avoid anything that increases agitation: leave the child on the caregiver's lap in the position they have chosen, offer blow-by oxygen if tolerated, and transport promptly. A is wrong because oropharyngeal suctioning stimulates the inflamed airway and can trigger laryngospasm and complete obstruction. B is wrong because forcing the child supine lets the swollen epiglottis fall back and occlude the airway, and one auscultation is not worth that risk. D is wrong because a conscious child will not tolerate an oropharyngeal airway, it provokes gagging and vomiting, and it does not bypass an obstruction above the glottis.
questions.explanationZh: 幼儿出现 stridor（喘鸣）、流涎并采取三脚架样前倾体位，提示 epiglottitis（会厌炎）等严重的声门上梗阻。此时肿胀的组织仅靠患儿自己选择的体位和平稳的呼吸努力维持着一条通道，因此首要原则是避免任何加重烦躁的操作：让孩子留在照护者怀中、保持其自选体位，能耐受时给予吹送式吸氧，并尽快转运。A 错误，口咽吸引会刺激已经发炎的气道，可能诱发喉痉挛和完全梗阻。B 错误，强行仰卧会让肿胀的会厌后坠堵住气道，为一次听诊冒这种风险并不值得。D 错误，清醒患儿无法耐受口咽通气道，置入会引起呕吐反射，而且它绕不过声门以上的梗阻。

questions.questionEn: A 32-year-old female at 36 weeks gestation complains of sudden, severe epigastric pain and blurred vision. Her blood pressure is 170/110 mmHg. Which interpretation of these findings is most accurate?
questions.questionZh: 一名 32 岁女性，妊娠 36 周，突发剧烈的上腹部疼痛并伴视物模糊，血压为 170/110 mmHg。对这些发现最准确的解读是什么？

options.en: The patient is exhibiting signs of severe preeclampsia
options.zh: 该患者出现了重度 preeclampsia（子痫前期）的表现

options.en: The patient is experiencing normal third-trimester discomfort
options.zh: 该患者只是妊娠晚期常见的正常不适

options.en: The patient is in the latent phase of labour
options.zh: 该患者处于产程的潜伏期

options.en: The patient is experiencing a simple gastrointestinal upset
options.zh: 该患者只是单纯的胃肠道不适

questions.explanationEn: Severe preeclampsia is new hypertension after 20 weeks gestation plus signs of end-organ involvement, and this patient has all three classic red flags at once: a pressure of 170/110, epigastric pain from stretching of the hepatic capsule, and visual disturbance from cerebral involvement. That combination can progress to an eclamptic seizure at any moment and demands calm handling, minimal stimulation and transport to an obstetric-capable facility. B is wrong because 170/110 is never a normal pregnancy reading and ordinary third-trimester discomfort does not cause visual change. C is wrong because latent labour presents with intermittent contractions, not sustained hypertension with visual symptoms. D is wrong because dismissing epigastric pain as indigestion is the classic error that delays recognition of impending eclampsia and HELLP syndrome.
questions.explanationZh: 重度 preeclampsia（子痫前期）的定义是妊娠 20 周后新发高血压加上靶器官受累的征象，而本例三个经典红旗同时出现：血压 170/110；肝包膜牵张引起的上腹痛；以及脑部受累导致的视觉障碍。这种组合随时可能进展为 eclampsia（子痫）抽搐，必须减少刺激、平稳处理并转运至具备产科能力的机构。B 错误，妊娠期 170/110 绝不属于正常，普通的妊娠晚期不适也不会引起视觉改变。C 错误，产程潜伏期表现为间歇性宫缩，而不是持续高血压合并视觉症状。D 错误，把上腹痛当成消化不良正是延误识别即将发生的子痫和 HELLP 综合征的典型错误。

questions.questionEn: A 55-year-old male complains of crushing chest pain and diaphoresis. The 12-lead ECG shows ST-segment elevation in leads II, III and aVF. The patient is hemodynamically stable. Which interpretation of this ECG finding is most accurate?
questions.questionZh: 一名 55 岁男性主诉压榨性胸痛并大汗淋漓。12 导联 ECG 显示 II、III、aVF 导联 ST 段抬高，患者血流动力学稳定。对这一 ECG 表现最准确的解读是什么？

options.en: The patient is experiencing an inferior wall myocardial infarction
options.zh: 该患者正在发生下壁心肌梗死（inferior wall myocardial infarction）

options.en: The patient is experiencing a posterior wall myocardial infarction
options.zh: 该患者正在发生后壁心肌梗死（posterior wall myocardial infarction）

options.en: The patient is experiencing a left bundle branch block
options.zh: 该患者出现的是左束支传导阻滞（left bundle branch block）

options.en: The patient is experiencing benign early repolarization
options.zh: 该患者出现的是良性早期复极（benign early repolarization）

questions.explanationEn: Leads II, III and aVF face the inferior wall, so ST elevation confined to exactly those three leads localises the infarct there, most often from right coronary artery occlusion. The localisation matters clinically because inferior infarcts frequently involve the right ventricle and produce bradyarrhythmias, which changes how nitroglycerin and fluids are handled. B is wrong because a true posterior infarct shows ST depression with tall R waves in V1-V3 rather than inferior elevation. C is wrong because left bundle branch block is a QRS abnormality - a wide QRS with discordant ST changes across many leads - not isolated inferior elevation. D is wrong because benign early repolarization gives diffuse, concave, notched J-point elevation in someone without ischemic symptoms, whereas this patient has crushing pain and diaphoresis.
questions.explanationZh: II、III、aVF 三个导联反映心脏下壁，因此 ST 段抬高恰好局限于这三个导联即可定位为下壁心肌梗死，最常见的责任血管是右冠状动脉。定位在临床上很重要，因为下壁梗死常合并右心室受累并出现缓慢性心律失常，这会改变 nitroglycerin（硝酸甘油）和补液的处理方式。B 错误，真正的后壁梗死表现为 V1–V3 导联 ST 段压低伴高 R 波，而不是下壁导联抬高。C 错误，左束支传导阻滞是 QRS 波异常——QRS 增宽并在多个导联出现与主波方向相反的 ST 改变——而非孤立的下壁抬高。D 错误，良性早期复极见于无缺血症状者，表现为弥漫性、凹面向上、J 点带切迹的抬高，而本例患者有压榨性疼痛和大汗。

questions.questionEn: A paramedic team is reviewing a new clinical guideline regarding neonatal resuscitation. Which action best demonstrates the application of evidence appraisal to their practice?
questions.questionZh: 一个急救团队正在审阅一份关于 neonatal resuscitation（新生儿复苏）的新版临床指南。哪一项做法最能体现把证据评价（evidence appraisal）应用到实践中？

options.en: Adopting the guideline because it was published by a well-known medical journal
options.zh: 因为它发表在知名医学期刊上就采纳该指南

options.en: Implementing the guideline immediately to ensure consistency with other crews
options.zh: 立即执行该指南，以便与其他班组保持一致

options.en: Following the guideline because it is the most recent version available
options.zh: 因为它是目前可获得的最新版本就照此执行

options.en: Comparing the guideline's recommendations against the strength of the supporting data
options.zh: 把指南的推荐意见与其背后支持数据的强度进行对照评估

questions.explanationEn: Appraising evidence means judging the quality and strength of the data behind a recommendation: study design, sample size, effect size, and whether the population studied resembles your patients. Only D describes that process. A is wrong because journal reputation is a proxy for quality, not evidence itself; prestigious journals still publish weak studies that are later refuted or retracted. B is wrong because crew-to-crew consistency is an operational goal and says nothing about whether a clinical claim is true. C is wrong because recency alone carries no information about quality - a new guideline may rest on expert consensus while an older one rests on randomised trials.
questions.explanationZh: 证据评价的含义是判断某条推荐背后数据的质量与强度：研究设计、样本量、效应量，以及所研究人群是否与自己面对的患者相似。只有 D 描述了这一过程。A 错误，期刊声誉只是质量的替代性指标而非证据本身，权威期刊同样会发表后来被推翻或撤稿的弱研究。B 错误，各班组做法一致属于运营层面的目标，与某项临床结论是否成立无关。C 错误，“最新”本身不携带任何质量信息——新指南可能只基于专家共识，旧指南却可能建立在随机对照试验之上。

questions.questionEn: During a handover to hospital staff, which communication technique best ensures the accurate transfer of critical patient information?
questions.questionZh: 在向医院工作人员交接患者时，哪种沟通方式最能确保关键患者信息被准确传递？

options.en: Providing a detailed narrative of the entire call in chronological order
options.zh: 按时间顺序把整个出勤过程详细叙述一遍

options.en: Allowing the receiving nurse to interrupt the report to ask questions
options.zh: 让接收护士随时打断报告提问

options.en: Using a structured format to present the patient's condition and interventions
options.zh: 使用结构化格式陈述患者状况和已实施的处置

options.en: Summarizing the patient's chief complaint and vital signs only
options.zh: 只概括患者的主诉和生命体征

questions.explanationEn: Structured handover formats such as IMIST-AMBO, MIST or SBAR fix both the order and the content of the report, so identification, mechanism, injuries or illness, signs, treatment given and the response to it are covered every time. That predictability is what measurably reduces omitted information and misunderstanding at transfer of care. A is wrong because an unstructured chronological narrative buries the critical items among incidental detail and takes far longer. B is wrong because uncontrolled interruptions fragment the report; questions belong after the structured report has been delivered. D is wrong because chief complaint and vital signs alone omit mechanism, treatments given and the patient's response - exactly the information the receiving team cannot reconstruct on its own.
questions.explanationZh: IMIST-AMBO、MIST、SBAR 这类结构化交接格式同时固定了报告的顺序和内容，使身份、受伤机制、伤情或病情、体征、已给处置及其反应每次都被覆盖到；正是这种可预期性能显著减少交接时的信息缺失和误解。A 错误，不加结构、按时间顺序的叙述会把关键信息淹没在枝节里，而且耗时得多。B 错误，不受控的打断会把报告切碎，提问应放在结构化报告讲完之后。D 错误，只讲主诉和生命体征会漏掉受伤机制、已给的治疗以及患者对治疗的反应，而这些恰恰是接收团队自己无法还原的信息。

questions.questionEn: A paramedic is assessing a newborn infant presenting with mild respiratory distress. Which finding is the most significant clinical indicator that the infant requires immediate escalation of care?
questions.questionZh: 一名急救员正在评估一名出现轻度呼吸窘迫的新生儿。下列哪项发现最能提示该新生儿需要立即升级处置？

options.en: A heart rate of 140 beats per minute
options.zh: 心率 140 次/分

options.en: Intercostal and subcostal retractions
options.zh: 肋间和肋下凹陷（retractions）

options.en: A respiratory rate of 50 breaths per minute
options.zh: 呼吸频率 50 次/分

options.en: The presence of vernix caseosa on the skin
options.zh: 皮肤上存在胎脂（vernix caseosa）

questions.explanationEn: A newborn's normal heart rate is roughly 120-160/min and a normal respiratory rate is roughly 40-60/min, so A and C are simply normal values, and vernix caseosa is normal skin covering with no respiratory meaning at all. Intercostal and subcostal retractions are abnormal at any age: they show the infant is generating large negative intrathoracic pressures just to move air, which signals markedly increased work of breathing in a patient with very little respiratory reserve. Retractions are therefore the finding that drives escalation to assisted ventilation and rapid transport before the infant tires and decompensates.
questions.explanationZh: 新生儿正常心率约 120–160 次/分，正常呼吸频率约 40–60 次/分，所以 A 和 C 只是正常值；胎脂（vernix caseosa）是正常的皮肤覆盖物，与呼吸完全无关。而肋间和肋下凹陷在任何年龄都属异常：它说明婴儿必须产生很大的胸腔负压才能把气吸进去，提示呼吸功明显增加，而新生儿的呼吸储备极其有限。因此凹陷才是那个应当促使你在婴儿力竭失代偿之前升级为辅助通气并快速转运的发现。

questions.questionEn: A 68-year-old patient reports a sudden onset of unilateral facial drooping and difficulty speaking, but all symptoms have completely resolved by the time the paramedic arrives. The patient's vital signs are within normal limits. What is the most appropriate clinical interpretation of this presentation?
questions.questionZh: 一名 68 岁患者主诉突发单侧面部下垂和言语困难，但在急救员到达时症状已完全缓解，生命体征均在正常范围。对这一表现最恰当的临床解读是什么？

options.en: Assume the symptoms were caused by a panic attack
options.zh: 认为症状是 panic attack（惊恐发作）所致

options.en: Recognize the presentation as a potential transient ischemic attack
options.zh: 将其识别为可能的 transient ischemic attack（TIA，短暂性脑缺血发作）

options.en: Advise the patient to return home and monitor for 24 hours
options.zh: 建议患者回家并自行观察 24 小时

options.en: Conclude that a normal blood glucose reading rules out any serious cause
options.zh: 认为血糖正常即可排除所有严重病因

questions.explanationEn: Focal neurological deficits that resolve completely are, by definition, a transient ischemic attack. A TIA is a warning rather than an all-clear: the risk of a completed stroke is highest in the first 48 hours, so this patient needs transport, pre-notification and urgent workup even though the examination is now normal. A is wrong because panic attacks do not produce unilateral facial droop and expressive speech difficulty. C is wrong and dangerous, because sending the patient home forfeits the narrow window in which secondary prevention can stop a disabling stroke. D is wrong because although a blood glucose check is a required part of the BC stroke assessment (hypoglycemia is the classic stroke mimic), a normal result does not exclude cerebral ischemia - it simply leaves TIA as the working diagnosis and does not change the transport decision.
questions.explanationZh: 完全缓解的局灶性神经功能缺损，按定义就是 transient ischemic attack（TIA，短暂性脑缺血发作）。TIA 是警报而不是解除警报：发生完全性卒中的风险在最初 48 小时内最高，所以即使此刻查体完全正常，仍必须转运、提前通知接收医院并接受紧急检查。A 错误，panic attack（惊恐发作）不会造成单侧面部下垂和表达性言语困难。C 错误且危险，让患者回家等于白白错过能够阻止致残性卒中的二级预防窗口。D 错误，血糖检测确实是 BC 卒中评估中必须做的一步（低血糖是经典的卒中模拟症），但结果正常并不能排除脑缺血——它只是让 TIA 仍然是工作诊断，并不改变转运决定。

questions.questionEn: While treating an adult patient, the paramedic discovers that the patient is a former colleague who is going through a difficult divorce. The patient begins to disclose intimate details about their marriage and asks the paramedic for personal advice on how to handle the legal separation. What is the most professional response?
questions.questionZh: 在救治一名成年患者时，急救员发现该患者是自己以前的同事，正经历痛苦的离婚。患者开始倾诉婚姻中的私密细节，并向急救员征求如何处理法律分居的个人建议。最专业的回应是什么？

options.en: Provide detailed legal and financial advice based on personal experience
options.zh: 根据自己的个人经验，提供详细的法律和财务建议

options.en: Listen empathetically while maintaining a professional boundary
options.zh: 共情地倾听，同时守住专业边界

options.en: Tell the patient to discuss the matter with their lawyer only
options.zh: 告诉患者这件事只能去和律师谈

options.en: Share personal stories about your own marriage to build rapport
options.zh: 分享自己婚姻中的故事来拉近关系

questions.explanationEn: Professional boundaries require the paramedic to stay inside the clinical role: acknowledge the distress, listen, and offer support without moving into a personal or advisory relationship. B does both at once - it keeps the therapeutic relationship intact while declining a role the paramedic is neither qualified nor positioned to take. A is wrong because legal and financial advice is outside any paramedic's scope and personal experience is not a basis for advising a patient. C is wrong because the word 'only' turns a reasonable referral into a brush-off that shuts down a distressed patient mid-disclosure. D is wrong because self-disclosure of this kind moves the focus onto the paramedic and erodes the very boundary that the pre-existing personal relationship already puts at risk.
questions.explanationZh: 专业边界要求急救员始终留在临床角色内：承认对方的痛苦、认真倾听、给予支持，但不进入私人关系或顾问角色。B 同时做到了这两点——既维持了治疗性关系，又拒绝承担自己既无资格也不该承担的角色。A 错误，法律和财务建议超出任何急救员的执业范围，个人经历也不能作为给患者出主意的依据。C 错误，“只能”这个词把一次合理的转介变成了打发，会让正在倾诉的患者当场闭嘴。D 错误，这类自我暴露会把焦点转移到急救员身上，进一步侵蚀本就因双方旧识关系而处于风险中的那条边界。

questions.questionEn: You are treating a 4-year-old child who is frightened and crying during a physical assessment. The child's parents are present and visibly anxious. Which communication strategy is most effective in this context?
questions.questionZh: 你正在为一名 4 岁儿童做体格检查，孩子因害怕而哭闹，在场的父母也明显焦虑。在这种情况下，哪种沟通策略最有效？

options.en: Get down to the child's eye level and explain the equipment using simple, non-threatening terms
options.zh: 蹲下来与孩子平视，用简单、不吓人的话解释你要用的器械

options.en: Instruct the parents to leave the room so the child can focus on the paramedic
options.zh: 请父母离开房间，好让孩子把注意力放在急救员身上

options.en: Tell the child that the procedure will not hurt to reduce their anxiety
options.zh: 告诉孩子“一点都不会痛”以减轻其焦虑

options.en: Perform the assessment quickly to minimize the child's distress
options.zh: 尽快把检查做完，以缩短孩子难受的时间

questions.explanationEn: A preschooler's fear is driven by size, strangeness and loss of control, so dropping to eye level removes the looming adult, and naming equipment in concrete, non-threatening words ('this is like a hug for your arm') restores predictability. A calm, cooperative child also yields a far more accurate respiratory and circulatory assessment. B is wrong because separating a 4-year-old from their caregiver removes the single greatest source of security and usually escalates the distress; the better move is to coach the anxious parent, not remove them. C is wrong because promising no pain destroys trust the moment something does hurt, and that loss of trust follows the child through every later encounter. D is wrong because rushing increases struggling and yields an unreliable examination; speed is warranted for a critically ill child, not for anxiety management.
questions.explanationZh: 学龄前儿童的恐惧主要来自体型差、陌生感和失控感，所以蹲下来与其平视可以消除“大人居高临下”的压迫，用具体而不吓人的话来称呼器械（比如“这个像给你的胳膊抱一下”）则能恢复可预期感。孩子平静配合后，你的呼吸和循环评估也会准确得多。B 错误，把 4 岁孩子和照护者分开等于拿走他最大的安全感来源，通常只会让哭闹升级；正确做法是安抚并指导焦虑的家长，而不是把家长请走。C 错误，承诺“不会痛”一旦被戳穿就彻底毁掉信任，而这种信任的丧失会一直影响孩子以后的每一次就医。D 错误，赶时间只会让孩子挣扎得更厉害、检查结果更不可靠；快速处置针对的是危重患儿，而不是用来对付焦虑。

questions.questionEn: While preparing to enter a residential building for a medical call, a paramedic notices a strong smell of natural gas and hears a faint hissing sound coming from the basement. Which action should the paramedic take first?
questions.questionZh: 在准备进入一栋住宅楼处理一起医疗呼叫时，急救员闻到浓烈的天然气气味，并听到地下室传来轻微的嘶嘶声。急救员首先应采取哪一项行动？

options.en: Enter the building and locate the gas shut-off valve
options.zh: 进入建筑物找到燃气总阀并关闭

options.en: Instruct the patient to evacuate the building immediately
options.zh: 指示患者立即自行撤离建筑物

options.en: Call the gas utility company to report the leak
options.zh: 致电燃气公司报告泄漏

options.en: Retreat to a safe distance and notify dispatch of the hazard
options.zh: 撤到安全距离外，并向调度报告该危险

questions.explanationEn: The Rescue Scene Evaluation exists to establish that the scene is safe for the crew and the patient before anything else happens, and an accumulating gas atmosphere is an explosive hazard that paramedics have neither the equipment nor the authority to control. Withdrawing and telling dispatch is the one action that both protects the crew and starts the correct resources - fire and the utility - moving. A is wrong because entering the building is exactly the exposure being avoided, and gas isolation is a fire service or utility task. B is wrong because it depends on a patient who may be unable to move or already obtunded, and it does not summon the resources needed. C is right in substance but wrong in sequence: notification goes through dispatch, who can simultaneously alert fire, the utility and other responding units, and it must follow withdrawal rather than precede it.
questions.explanationZh: 救援现场评估（Rescue Scene Evaluation）的存在意义，就是在做任何其他事之前先确认现场对救护人员和患者都是安全的；而不断积聚的燃气构成爆炸性危险，急救员既没有装备也没有权限去处置它。撤离并通知调度是唯一一个既保护班组、又能同时让正确资源（消防和燃气公司）动起来的动作。A 错误，进入建筑正是你要避免的暴露，切断燃气是消防或燃气公司的任务。B 错误，它把希望寄托在一个可能根本走不动或已意识模糊的患者身上，而且没有调来任何所需资源。C 内容本身没错但顺序错了：通知要经调度发出，由调度同时联系消防、燃气公司和其他出动单位，而且必须在撤离之后而不是之前。

questions.questionEn: A paramedic has been working a series of extended shifts during a local emergency and is experiencing cognitive fog and slowed reaction times while caring for patients. Which factor most directly affects this paramedic's fitness to practise?
questions.questionZh: 某急救员因当地突发事件连续加班，已连做数个超长班次，在照护患者时出现思维迟钝和反应变慢。哪一项因素最直接地影响该急救员当下的执业适任性（fitness to practise）？

options.en: The age of the patients being treated
options.zh: 所救治患者的年龄

options.en: The complexity of the medical equipment used
options.zh: 所使用医疗设备的复杂程度

options.en: The availability of backup personnel
options.zh: 是否有后备人员可供调用

options.en: The cumulative effect of sleep deprivation
options.zh: 睡眠剥夺的累积效应

questions.explanationEn: Fitness to practise is a property of the practitioner, not of the call. Cumulative sleep debt degrades vigilance, working memory and reaction time in a dose-dependent way, and the impaired clinician characteristically underestimates their own deficit - which is why the framework places an affirmative duty on paramedics to monitor themselves and to remove themselves from practice when they can no longer self-regulate or perform safely. A is wrong because patient age changes the clinical demands of the call but not the paramedic's own capacity. B is wrong for the same reason: equipment complexity is a task factor that fatigue makes harder to manage, not the underlying cause of the impairment. C is wrong because backup availability determines what mitigations exist after impairment is recognised; it does not determine whether the paramedic is currently fit.
questions.explanationZh: 执业适任性说的是从业者本人的状态，而不是这趟任务的性质。累积的睡眠债会以剂量相关的方式削弱警觉性、工作记忆和反应速度，而受损的临床人员典型地会低估自己的受损程度——正因如此，能力框架才明确要求急救员主动监测自身状态，并在无法自我调节、无法安全执业时把自己撤下来。A 错误，患者年龄改变的是这趟任务的临床难度，而不是急救员自身的能力。B 同理错误，设备复杂度是任务因素，疲劳会让它更难应付，但它不是损害的根源。C 错误，是否有后备人员决定的是识别到损害之后能采取哪些补救，而不能决定此刻该急救员是否适任。

questions.questionEn: A paramedic is treating a patient in a low-income neighbourhood who frequently calls 911 for chronic conditions because they have no reliable transportation to a primary care clinic. Which community resource would best address this patient's long-term health outcomes?
questions.questionZh: 一名急救员在低收入社区救治一位患者，该患者因为没有可靠的交通工具前往基层诊所，经常为慢性病拨打 911。哪一项社区资源最能改善这位患者的长期健康结局？

options.en: Increasing the frequency of emergency response units in the area
options.zh: 增加该地区急救车辆的出动频次

options.en: Connecting the patient with a community-based mobile health clinic
options.zh: 把患者对接到社区流动医疗诊所

options.en: Providing the patient with a list of nearby hospitals
options.zh: 给患者一份附近医院的清单

options.en: Advising the patient to call 911 only for life-threatening emergencies
options.zh: 劝告患者只在危及生命时才打 911

questions.explanationEn: The barrier here is named explicitly: the patient cannot physically reach primary care. A mobile clinic removes exactly that barrier by bringing longitudinal chronic-disease management to the patient, which is what changes long-term outcomes and, incidentally, reduces the repeat 911 use. A is wrong because more ambulances treat the symptom of the problem - repeated emergency contacts - while leaving the access gap untouched. C is wrong because a list of hospitals is useless to someone whose problem is transportation, and hospitals do not provide continuity of chronic care. D is wrong because it simply withdraws the only service the patient can currently reach, shifting risk onto the patient rather than addressing the determinant.
questions.explanationZh: 本题的障碍已经写明：患者在物理上到不了基层医疗。流动诊所恰好消除的正是这个障碍——把慢性病的连续性管理送到患者身边，这才是改变长期结局的做法，同时也顺带减少了重复呼叫 911。A 错误，增加救护车只是在处理问题的表象（反复呼叫急救），却完全没有触碰可及性这道缺口。C 错误，对一个问题出在交通上的人来说，医院清单毫无用处，而且医院也不提供慢性病的连续管理。D 错误，这等于把患者目前唯一能够触及的服务也撤走，是把风险转嫁给患者，而不是去处理那个决定因素。

questions.questionEn: A 55-year-old patient presents with sudden onset of severe chest pain, diaphoresis and shortness of breath, and has a history of hypertension and diabetes. After confirming there are no allergies or other contraindications, which intervention is most appropriate to initiate first?
questions.questionZh: 一名 55 岁患者突发剧烈胸痛、大汗和呼吸困难，既往有高血压和糖尿病史。在确认无过敏及其他禁忌后，最应当首先实施的干预是哪一项？

options.en: Administer a platelet inhibitor as per local protocol
options.zh: 按当地方案给予血小板抑制剂（ASA）

options.en: Perform a 12-lead ECG and withhold treatment until a physician interprets it
options.zh: 做 12 导联 ECG，并在医生判读之前暂不给予治疗

options.en: Assist the patient with their own prescribed vasodilator before obtaining vital signs
options.zh: 在测量生命体征之前先协助患者使用其自备的血管扩张剂

options.en: Initiate high-flow oxygen therapy via non-rebreather mask for all chest pain
options.zh: 对所有胸痛患者一律经非重复呼吸面罩给予高流量氧

questions.explanationEn: In the BC cardiac chest pain protocol, acetylsalicylic acid chewed and swallowed is an all-licence-level intervention delivered early, and ASA is the one drug for which a set of vital signs is not required beforehand - precisely so that antiplatelet therapy is not delayed while assessment continues. B is wrong because although the 12-lead should be obtained, treatment is not held pending physician interpretation; the protocol is standing and time-critical. C is wrong on sequence and safety: nitroglycerin does follow in the protocol, but only after baseline vitals, because BC contraindicates it when the systolic pressure is below 110 mmHg, the heart rate is under 50 or over 150, or a PDE-5 inhibitor has been used recently. D is wrong because oxygen is titrated to maintain an SpO2 of at least 94%, not given routinely at high flow to every chest-pain patient.
questions.explanationZh: 在 BC 的心源性胸痛方案中，嚼服并咽下 acetylsalicylic acid（ASA，阿司匹林）属于所有执照等级都可实施的早期干预，而且 ASA 是唯一一个给药前不要求先测生命体征的药物——设计初衷正是为了不让抗血小板治疗被评估流程拖住。B 错误，12 导联该做，但不能把治疗压着等医生判读，该方案是常设的、时间敏感的。C 在顺序和安全性上都错：nitroglycerin（硝酸甘油）在方案中确实随后出场，但必须先有基线生命体征，因为 BC 规定收缩压低于 110 mmHg、心率低于 50 或高于 150、以及近期使用过 PDE-5 抑制剂时禁用。D 错误，氧疗应滴定到 SpO2 ≥ 94%，而不是对每一位胸痛患者都常规高流量给氧。

questions.questionEn: During a complex pediatric cardiac arrest, a paramedic observes a senior partner deviate from the local clinical practice guidelines without any clinical justification. Which action best reflects professional accountability?
questions.questionZh: 在一次复杂的儿科心脏骤停抢救中，某急救员发现资深搭档在没有任何临床理由的情况下偏离了当地临床实践指南。哪一项做法最能体现专业问责？

options.en: Follow the partner's lead to maintain scene flow
options.zh: 跟着搭档走，以免打乱现场节奏

options.en: Document the deviation in the patient care report for later review
options.zh: 把偏离写进病历报告，留待事后审查

options.en: Respectfully question the partner during the resuscitation to protect the patient
options.zh: 在复苏过程中即时、有礼貌地向搭档提出疑问，以保护患者

options.en: Wait until the debriefing to discuss the deviation with the partner
options.zh: 等到事后汇报时再和搭档讨论这次偏离

questions.explanationEn: Accountability is owed to the patient in front of you, and during a resuscitation the only intervention that can still change the outcome is one made now. Raising the concern respectfully and specifically in the moment gives the partner the chance to explain a reason you may not have seen, or to correct course before harm occurs. A is wrong because deferring to seniority when patient safety is at stake is precisely the failure mode that closed-loop, speak-up culture exists to prevent. B is wrong because documentation is a necessary record but is not a substitute for intervention; writing it down afterwards does nothing for this child. D is wrong for the same reason - a debrief addresses future practice, not the patient who is being harmed now, although a debrief should still follow once the call is over.
questions.explanationZh: 问责首先是对眼前这位患者负责，而在复苏进行中，唯一还可能改变结局的干预就是此刻做出的干预。当场、有礼貌且具体地提出疑问，既给了搭档解释你可能没看到的理由的机会，也可能在造成伤害之前把方向纠正过来。A 错误，在患者安全受威胁时因资历而退让，正是“敢于发声”文化要防止的那种失效模式。B 错误，记录是必要的留痕，但不能替代干预；事后写下来对这个孩子没有任何帮助。D 错误同理——事后汇报处理的是今后的实践，而不是此刻正在受损的患者；当然，任务结束后仍应进行汇报。

questions.questionEn: A newborn is delivered in the field and is not breathing or crying. After 30 seconds of drying, stimulation and keeping the infant warm, the infant remains apneic with a heart rate of 80 beats per minute. What is the most appropriate next step?
questions.questionZh: 一名新生儿在院外娩出，无呼吸也无哭声。在完成 30 秒的擦干、刺激和保暖后，该新生儿仍无呼吸，心率为 80 次/分。下一步最恰当的处理是什么？

options.en: Initiate chest compressions
options.zh: 开始胸外按压

options.en: Begin ventilation with a bag-valve mask
options.zh: 开始用球囊面罩（BVM）进行通气

options.en: Administer a sympathomimetic
options.zh: 给予拟交感药物

options.en: Perform rapid endotracheal intubation
options.zh: 迅速进行气管插管

questions.explanationEn: The BC newborn sequence is stepwise and driven by heart rate. Step 1 is dry, stimulate and keep warm for 30 seconds; if the heart rate is still under 100 you move to step 2, which is bag-valve-mask ventilation on room air for 30 seconds, then step 3 adds 100% oxygen. Almost every neonatal arrest is hypoxic in origin, so ventilation is the intervention that reverses it. A is wrong because compressions only begin at step 4, after ventilation with 100% oxygen has failed to raise the heart rate; the BC guideline continues compressions with ventilations until the heart rate is above 60. C is wrong because a sympathomimetic is not part of the BC newborn sequence at this level and treats neither the hypoxia nor the apnea. D is wrong because endotracheal intubation is outside the PCP scope of practice and would delay the effective intervention.
questions.explanationZh: BC 的新生儿处理顺序是分步进行、由心率驱动的。第 1 步是擦干、刺激、保暖 30 秒；若心率仍低于 100 次/分，进入第 2 步——用球囊面罩以室内空气通气 30 秒；仍低于 100 则进入第 3 步，改接 100% 氧。新生儿骤停几乎都源于缺氧，所以通气才是能扭转局面的干预。A 错误，按压要到第 4 步才开始，即在 100% 氧通气仍不能把心率提上来之后；BC 考纲规定按压加通气持续到心率高于 60 次/分。C 错误，拟交感药物不在本级别的 BC 新生儿处理顺序内，既不解决缺氧也不解决呼吸暂停。D 错误，气管插管超出 PCP 执业范围，而且会延误真正有效的干预。

questions.questionEn: A paramedic notices a recurring pattern of falls among geriatric patients at one particular long-term care facility. To improve patient outcomes and professional practice, what is the most appropriate action?
questions.questionZh: 一名急救员注意到某家长期照护机构反复出现老年患者跌倒的情况。为改善患者结局并提升专业实践，最恰当的做法是什么？

options.en: Inform the patients that the facility is unsafe
options.zh: 告诉患者们这家机构不安全

options.en: Request that the facility hire more staff
options.zh: 要求该机构增聘人手

options.en: Document the falls in the individual patient charts only
options.zh: 只把每次跌倒记录在各自的病历里

options.en: Collaborate with the facility's clinical lead to review fall-prevention strategies
options.zh: 与该机构的临床负责人合作，共同检讨跌倒预防策略

questions.explanationEn: A pattern seen across many calls is exactly the kind of signal a single clinician is uniquely placed to notice and no single chart will reveal. Turning that observation into an improvement conversation with the people who control the environment - flooring, footwear, toileting routines, medication timing, staffing at night - is what converts an observation into fewer falls. A is wrong because it alarms residents, damages a working relationship and gives them no means to act. B is wrong because it prescribes one solution before the causes are understood, and staffing may not be the driver at all. C is wrong because chart-level documentation is necessary but keeps the pattern invisible; nobody aggregates individual charts across services, so the trend never reaches anyone who can act on it.
questions.explanationZh: 跨多次出勤才浮现的规律，恰恰是一线临床人员最有条件察觉、而任何单份病历都看不出来的信号。把这个观察变成一次与掌握环境的人（地面、鞋具、如厕流程、给药时间、夜班人力）之间的改进对话，才是把观察转化为“跌倒减少”的路径。A 错误，这会让住户恐慌、破坏合作关系，而且他们本身也无从改变。B 错误，在病因还没弄清之前就先开出唯一的药方，而人手未必是真正的动因。C 错误，病历层面的记录是必要的，但会让规律始终隐形——没有人会把各机构的单份病历汇总起来，趋势因此永远传不到能采取行动的人手里。

questions.questionEn: A conscious, hemodynamically stable adult patient refuses a recommended life-saving intervention. After the paramedic explains the risks of refusal and the benefits of the procedure, the patient continues to decline. What is the most appropriate next step?
questions.questionZh: 一名意识清醒、血流动力学稳定的成年患者拒绝接受推荐的救命干预。急救员已经说明拒绝的风险和该操作的获益后，患者仍然拒绝。下一步最恰当的做法是什么？

options.en: Administer the intervention and document the patient's verbal protest
options.zh: 照样实施该干预，并在记录中写明患者口头反对

options.en: Ask the patient's next of kin to provide consent on their behalf
options.zh: 请患者的近亲属代为签署同意

options.en: Respect the patient's autonomous decision and document the refusal
options.zh: 尊重患者的自主决定，并完整记录这次拒绝

options.en: Contact the receiving hospital for a physician's order to override the refusal
options.zh: 联系接收医院，取得医嘱以推翻患者的拒绝

questions.explanationEn: A capable adult may refuse any intervention, including one that will save their life, and the paramedic's obligation ends at ensuring the refusal is informed. Once risks and benefits have been explained and the patient still declines, the correct action is to accept the decision and document it thoroughly: what was offered, what risks were explained, evidence the patient understood them, who witnessed the refusal, and the advice given about calling back. A is wrong because treating over a capable patient's objection is battery, and documenting the protest does not make it lawful. B is wrong because a substitute decision-maker only has authority when the patient lacks capacity; family cannot override a capable adult. D is wrong because no physician order can authorise treatment that a capable patient has refused.
questions.explanationZh: 有决策能力的成年人可以拒绝任何干预，包括救命的干预，而急救员的义务止于确保这次拒绝是“知情”的。在已经说明风险与获益、患者仍然拒绝之后，正确做法是接受这一决定并做详尽记录：提供了什么、说明了哪些风险、有哪些证据显示患者理解了、谁在场见证、以及你就“如需帮助请再次呼叫”给出的建议。A 错误，在有能力患者明确反对下仍施加治疗构成人身侵害，把反对写进记录并不能让它合法。B 错误，替代决策者只有在患者丧失决策能力时才有权限，家属无法推翻一个有能力成年人的决定。D 错误，任何医嘱都无法授权实施一位有能力患者已经拒绝的治疗。

questions.questionEn: An 82-year-old patient is found confused and lethargic by family. The patient has a history of type 2 diabetes and hypertension, and still protects their own airway. The blood glucose reads 3.2 mmol/L. Which action is most appropriate?
questions.questionZh: 一名 82 岁患者被家人发现意识混乱、嗜睡，既往有 2 型糖尿病和高血压病史，目前仍能自行保护气道。血糖读数为 3.2 mmol/L。哪一项处理最恰当？

options.en: Administer a sympathomimetic to increase the heart rate
options.zh: 给予拟交感药物以提升心率

options.en: Initiate a primary survey to identify other injuries
options.zh: 开始进行初步检查（primary survey）以寻找其他损伤

options.en: Prepare a non-narcotic analgesic for the patient's discomfort
options.zh: 准备非麻醉性镇痛药以缓解患者的不适

options.en: Administer a carbohydrate in a form the patient can safely swallow
options.zh: 以患者能安全吞咽的形式给予碳水化合物

questions.explanationEn: A blood glucose of 3.2 mmol/L is below the BC treatment threshold of 4.0 mmol/L, and it fully explains the confusion and lethargy. The BC diabetic emergency guideline directs that hypoglycemia be corrected, and for a patient with sufficient mentation to protect their own airway that means glucose gel applied to the oral mucosa; oral glucose is authorised only where there is no risk of aspiration or choking, which is why the route must be matched to the level of consciousness rather than assumed. A is wrong because heart rate is not the problem and a sympathomimetic does nothing for neuroglycopenia. B is wrong on timing: the primary survey has already been completed - that is how the glucose was obtained - and searching for further injuries before correcting a documented, reversible cause of the altered mentation leaves the patient hypoglycemic for longer. C is wrong because analgesia treats neither the hypoglycemia nor the altered mentation and adds sedation risk.
questions.explanationZh: 血糖 3.2 mmol/L 低于 BC 规定的 4.0 mmol/L 处理阈值，并且足以解释患者的意识混乱和嗜睡。BC 的糖尿病急症指南要求纠正低血糖，对于神志尚足以自行保护气道的患者，做法是把葡萄糖凝胶涂在口腔黏膜上；口服葡萄糖只有在不存在误吸或窒息风险时才获授权，所以给药途径必须与意识水平相匹配，而不能想当然。A 错误，心率并不是问题所在，拟交感药物对脑内葡萄糖缺乏毫无作用。B 错在时机：初步检查其实已经做完（血糖正是这一步测出来的），在已经查明且可逆的意识改变病因面前先去搜寻其他损伤，只会让患者的低血糖状态持续更久。C 错误，镇痛既不解决低血糖也不解决意识改变，还额外带来镇静风险。

questions.questionEn: A paramedic is called to a community where a significant portion of the population identifies as Indigenous. During the assessment, the paramedic notices that the patient's family are using traditional healing practices alongside the care being provided. Which approach best demonstrates culturally safe care?
questions.questionZh: 一名急救员前往一个原住民人口占相当比例的社区出勤。在评估过程中，急救员注意到患者家属正在与急救处置同时进行传统疗愈仪式。哪一种做法最能体现文化安全（cultural safety）的护理？

options.en: Incorporating the patient's traditional practices into the care plan while ensuring medical safety
options.zh: 在确保医疗安全的前提下，把患者的传统实践纳入护理计划

options.en: Asking the family to pause traditional practices until the patient reaches hospital
options.zh: 请家属暂停传统实践，等患者到院后再说

options.en: Explaining to the patient why Western medicine is the primary evidence-based choice
options.zh: 向患者解释为什么西医才是首选的循证方案

options.en: Documenting the traditional practices as a secondary concern in the patient report
options.zh: 把传统实践作为次要事项记录在病历报告中

questions.explanationEn: Cultural safety is judged by the patient, not the provider, and it asks whether care was delivered without stripping the patient of their own understanding of healing. Where a practice does not interfere with assessment or treatment - smudging, prayer, the presence of an Elder, a family member holding a medicine bundle - it can proceed alongside clinical care, and accommodating it typically increases cooperation with the clinical plan rather than competing with it. The qualifier 'while ensuring medical safety' is what keeps this from being uncritical: a practice that would delay a time-critical intervention still has to be negotiated. B is wrong because pausing a practice that causes no clinical harm asserts authority for its own sake and reproduces the very exclusion that culturally safe practice is meant to undo. C is wrong because ranking knowledge systems for the patient is a lecture, not care, and predictably reduces engagement. D is wrong because relegating the practice to a footnote acknowledges it on paper while changing nothing about how the patient is actually treated.
questions.explanationZh: 文化安全的评判者是患者而不是医疗人员，它追问的是：这次照护有没有剥夺患者自己对“疗愈”的理解。当某项实践并不妨碍评估或治疗时——熏香净化、祈祷、长者在场、家人手持药包——它完全可以与临床处置并行，而且迁就它通常会提高患者对临床方案的配合度，而不是与之竞争。“在确保医疗安全的前提下”这个限定语正是本题不流于盲从的关键：若某项实践会延误时间敏感的干预，仍必须协商。B 错误，叫停一项并不造成临床危害的实践，只是为了行使权威，重现了文化安全本要消解的那种排斥。C 错误，替患者给不同知识体系排座次是说教而不是照护，可预见地会降低其参与度。D 错误，把它降格为记录里的次要事项，等于在纸面上承认，却丝毫没有改变患者实际被对待的方式。

questions.questionEn: A paramedic is dispatched to a person in a mental health crisis who is pacing rapidly and shouting incoherently. The person is not physically aggressive but appears highly agitated. Which intervention is the most appropriate initial action to de-escalate the situation?
questions.questionZh: 一名急救员被派往处理一位处于精神健康危机中的人，该人快速踱步、语无伦次地大喊，没有肢体攻击行为，但显得极度激越。作为去激越（de-escalation）的初始处置，哪一项最恰当？

options.en: Instructing the person to sit down and remain quiet
options.zh: 命令该人坐下并保持安静

options.en: Using a calm, non-threatening tone and maintaining a safe distance
options.zh: 使用平静、不具威胁性的语气，并保持安全距离

options.en: Requesting immediate police assistance to restrain the person
options.zh: 立即请求警方到场将其约束

options.en: Asking the person to repeat their statements more clearly
options.zh: 要求该人把话说得更清楚一些、重复一遍

questions.explanationEn: An agitated person is operating on threat perception, so the intervention has to lower perceived threat before anything else can work. A slow, low, unhurried voice and a generous interpersonal distance signal that you are not going to grab them, which is what allows arousal to fall far enough for assessment and consent to become possible. A is wrong because a command asserts control over someone who is already feeling controlled, and non-compliance then reads as escalation to everyone present. C is wrong because restraint is a last resort for imminent danger; this person is agitated but not aggressive, and involving officers to restrain at this stage converts a health encounter into a confrontation and forfeits any therapeutic relationship. D is wrong because pressing someone whose thinking is disorganised to perform clearly on demand increases frustration and arousal; you gather history after arousal comes down, not before.
questions.explanationZh: 处于激越状态的人是靠“威胁感知”在运作的，所以干预必须先把感知到的威胁降下来，其他事情才可能奏效。缓慢、低沉、不催促的语调加上足够宽裕的人际距离，传递的信息是“我不会扑上来抓你”，这才让唤醒水平下降到足以进行评估、也足以谈得上同意的程度。A 错误，对一个本来就感到被控制的人下命令，是在强化控制，而他一旦不服从，在所有在场者眼里就变成了“升级”。C 错误，约束是针对迫在眉睫危险的最后手段；此人激越但无攻击行为，此时叫警察来约束，会把一次医疗接触变成对峙，也断送了任何治疗性关系。D 错误，逼一个思维已经紊乱的人“说清楚点”只会加重挫败和唤醒；采集病史应放在唤醒水平降下来之后，而不是之前。

questions.questionEn: A 68-year-old patient complains of mild shortness of breath. The 12-lead ECG shows a normal sinus rate with a consistent PR interval of 0.24 seconds, and every P wave is followed by a QRS complex. What is the most accurate interpretation of this finding?
questions.questionZh: 一名 68 岁患者主诉轻度呼吸困难。12 导联 ECG 显示窦性心律、频率正常，PR 间期恒定为 0.24 秒，且每一个 P 波后面都跟着一个 QRS 波。对这一发现最准确的解读是什么？

options.en: Second-degree AV block, Mobitz Type I
options.zh: 二度房室传导阻滞，Mobitz I 型

options.en: Second-degree AV block, Mobitz Type II
options.zh: 二度房室传导阻滞，Mobitz II 型

options.en: Third-degree AV block
options.zh: 三度（完全性）房室传导阻滞

options.en: First-degree AV block
options.zh: 一度房室传导阻滞

questions.explanationEn: First-degree AV block is defined by a PR interval longer than 0.20 seconds that is constant from beat to beat, with every atrial impulse still conducted to the ventricles. A PR of 0.24 seconds with a QRS after every P wave meets that definition exactly, and it is usually a benign, chronic finding that is not the cause of this patient's dyspnea - so it must not distract from looking for the real reason. A is wrong because Mobitz I shows progressive PR lengthening ending in a dropped QRS; here the interval never changes and nothing is dropped. B is wrong because Mobitz II shows a constant PR with intermittently dropped QRS complexes; here no beat is dropped. C is wrong because third-degree block means complete AV dissociation with P waves and QRS complexes marching independently, whereas this tracing shows a fixed, consistent relationship between them.
questions.explanationZh: 一度房室传导阻滞的定义是 PR 间期长于 0.20 秒且逐搏恒定，同时每一次心房激动仍能下传心室。PR 为 0.24 秒且每个 P 波后都有 QRS，恰好符合这一定义；它通常是良性的慢性表现，并不是这位患者呼吸困难的原因——因此绝不能让它把你的注意力从真正的病因上引开。A 错误，Mobitz I 型表现为 PR 间期逐搏延长直至脱落一个 QRS；本例 PR 从不改变，也没有脱落。B 错误，Mobitz II 型表现为 PR 恒定但间断脱落 QRS；本例没有任何一搏脱落。C 错误，三度阻滞意味着完全性房室分离，P 波与 QRS 各走各的，而本图显示两者之间存在固定不变的对应关系。

questions.questionEn: When assessing an adult patient with suspected opioid overdose, which clinical finding is the most critical indicator for administering an opioid antagonist?
questions.questionZh: 在评估一名疑似阿片类药物过量的成年患者时，哪一项临床发现是给予阿片拮抗剂最关键的指征？

options.en: Respiratory depression
options.zh: 呼吸抑制

options.en: Pinpoint pupils
options.zh: 针尖样瞳孔

options.en: Bradycardia
options.zh: 心动过缓

options.en: Hypotension
options.zh: 低血压

questions.explanationEn: The BC indication for naloxone is to reverse respiratory depression or depressed mental status secondary to actual or suspected narcotic use, and the dosing ladder is titrated to a specific respiratory endpoint - repeat doses are given only until an SpO2 of at least 94% and a respiratory rate above 10 are achieved. Respiratory failure is what kills in opioid toxicity, so it is both the reason to give the drug and the measure of whether enough has been given. B is wrong because miosis is a supporting sign that helps you recognise the toxidrome but is not itself dangerous; a patient with pinpoint pupils who is ventilating adequately does not need naloxone. C and D are wrong for the same reason: hypotension is listed as an associated feature and bradycardia usually reflects the hypoxia rather than the opioid itself, and neither is titrated against naloxone dosing. Chasing pupils or blood pressure instead of ventilation risks precipitating agitated withdrawal in a patient who was never in respiratory danger.
questions.explanationZh: BC 对 naloxone（纳洛酮）的指征是逆转由确证或疑似麻醉品使用所致的呼吸抑制或意识抑制，而其剂量阶梯是按一个明确的呼吸终点滴定的——只有在 SpO2 未达到 ≥94%、呼吸频率未超过 10 次/分时才重复给药。阿片中毒致死的机制是呼吸衰竭，所以呼吸抑制既是给药的理由，也是判断“给够了没有”的标尺。B 错误，瞳孔缩小是帮助你识别该中毒综合征的支持性体征，本身并不危险；一个针尖瞳孔但通气充分的患者并不需要 naloxone。C 和 D 同理错误：低血压属于伴随表现，心动过缓通常反映的是缺氧而非阿片本身，两者都不作为 naloxone 的滴定目标。盯着瞳孔或血压而不是通气来给药，可能让一个本无呼吸危险的患者被诱发出激越的戒断反应。

questions.questionEn: When transferring an elderly patient with complex comorbidities and multiple medications to hospital staff, which information is most critical to include in the handover to ensure continuity of care?
questions.questionZh: 在把一位合并多种疾病、服用多种药物的老年患者交接给医院工作人员时，哪一项信息对确保护理连续性最为关键？

options.en: The patient's total number of previous hospital admissions
options.zh: 患者既往住院次数的总数

options.en: The patient's current mental status and recent changes from their baseline cognition
options.zh: 患者当前的精神状态，以及相对于其基线认知的近期变化

options.en: The patient's primary language and preferred pronouns
options.zh: 患者的主要语言和偏好的人称代词

options.en: The patient's long-term living arrangements and social support system
options.zh: 患者的长期居住安排和社会支持体系

questions.explanationEn: In a complex older patient, a single mental status reading is nearly meaningless to the receiving team because they have no way of knowing what this person is normally like. The delta - what has changed, and over what time frame - is the finding that separates chronic dementia from an acute delirium caused by infection, hypoxia, drug effect or metabolic derangement, and you are often the only clinician who has spoken to family and seen the home. A is wrong because a raw admission count carries no clinical decision value. C and D are genuinely useful for communication and discharge planning respectively, and both belong in a full report, but neither changes the immediate diagnostic or resuscitation priorities the way an acute change in cognition does.
questions.explanationZh: 对于情况复杂的老年患者，孤立的一次精神状态描述对接收团队几乎没有意义，因为他们无从知道这个人平时是什么样子。真正有价值的是“变化量”——变了什么、在多长时间内变的——这正是区分慢性痴呆与由感染、缺氧、药物或代谢紊乱引起的急性谵妄的关键，而你往往是唯一一个跟家属谈过、也见过家中环境的临床人员。A 错误，单纯的住院次数不承载任何临床决策价值。C 和 D 分别对沟通和出院规划确有用处，也都应出现在完整报告里，但它们都不像“认知的急性改变”那样能立即改变诊断和抢救优先级。

questions.questionEn: While responding to a call for an unconscious adult in a public park, the paramedic finds several items of drug paraphernalia and notices a strong chemical odour. Which action best demonstrates the application of scene safety standards in this context?
questions.questionZh: 在前往公园处理一名成年人昏迷的呼叫时，急救员发现现场有若干吸毒用具，并闻到浓烈的化学气味。在这种情境下，哪一项做法最能体现现场安全标准的应用？

options.en: Donning appropriate personal protective equipment before approaching the patient
options.zh: 在接近患者之前先穿戴合适的个人防护装备（PPE）

options.en: Requesting immediate police assistance to clear the area of bystanders
options.zh: 立即请求警方到场清走围观人群

options.en: Instructing the patient to move to a safer location before assessment
options.zh: 在评估前指示患者移动到更安全的位置

options.en: Performing a rapid primary survey to determine the need for transport
options.zh: 先做快速初步检查以判断是否需要转运

questions.explanationEn: Scene evaluation exists to protect the crew before patient contact, and the two findings here - sharps and an unidentified chemical odour - name the two exposures precisely: needlestick injury and inhalational or dermal contact. Gloves, eye protection and a respiratory barrier take seconds and are the only measures that make the subsequent patient contact safe. B is wrong because bystanders are not the hazard described, and while police may be requested, waiting on them is not the immediate protective step. C is wrong because the patient is unconscious and cannot follow instructions - a detail that also should prompt you to re-read the scene rather than the patient. D is wrong because it inverts the order: the primary survey is essential but requires contact, and making contact before protection is exactly the failure the scene evaluation is designed to prevent.
questions.explanationZh: 现场评估的意义在于在接触患者之前先保护班组，而本题的两个发现——锐器和来源不明的化学气味——恰好点名了两类暴露：针刺伤，以及吸入或皮肤接触。戴手套、护目和呼吸防护只需要几秒钟，却是让随后的患者接触变得安全的唯一措施。B 错误，围观者并不是题干描述的危险；即使需要请警方到场，等警察也不是眼下的防护步骤。C 错误，患者已经昏迷、无法执行指令——这个细节本身也提示你该重新审视的是现场而不是患者。D 错误，它把顺序颠倒了：初步检查确实必不可少，但它需要接触患者，而在防护之前就接触，正是现场评估要防止的那种失误。

questions.questionEn: During a mass casualty incident, a Primary Care Paramedic has completed the initial triage of several patients. When a second crew arrives to assist, what is the most appropriate method for sharing patient information to ensure continuity of care?
questions.questionZh: 在一起大规模伤亡事件中，一名 PCP 已完成对多名伤员的初次分诊。当第二组人员到场支援时，采用哪种方式传递患者信息最能确保护理的连续性？

options.en: Verbally describing the general condition of all patients on scene
options.zh: 口头描述现场所有伤员的大致状况

options.en: Allowing the arriving crew to perform their own independent triage
options.zh: 让到场的第二组自行重新独立分诊

options.en: Directing the arriving crew to the most critical patient first
options.zh: 先把到场的第二组带到最危重的伤员那里

options.en: Using standardized triage tags to communicate patient priority and status
options.zh: 使用标准化分诊标签来传达伤员的优先级和状态

questions.explanationEn: In a multiple-patient incident, information has to survive changes of personnel, noise, darkness and the original triager moving on. A tag physically attached to the patient does exactly that: it travels with the patient, records category, time and findings, and lets any arriving crew read priority off the patient without a conversation. A is wrong because a verbal summary of many patients cannot be retained accurately, cannot be re-checked, and evaporates the moment the person who gave it is reassigned. B is wrong because repeating triage from scratch wastes the scarcest resource in an MCI - time - and produces inconsistent categories between crews. C is not wrong as an action and often happens anyway, but it addresses only one patient and leaves the status of everyone else unrecorded, which is the opposite of continuity across the whole scene.
questions.explanationZh: 在多伤员事件中，信息必须能够扛住人员轮换、噪音、光线不足，以及最初分诊者离开现场。物理挂在伤员身上的分诊标签正好做到这一点：它随伤员一起走，记录了类别、时间和发现，让任何到场的班组不必对话就能直接从伤员身上读出优先级。A 错误，对多名伤员的口头概述无法被准确记住、无法回查，一旦讲述者被调走就随之消失。B 错误，从头重做分诊消耗的正是 MCI 中最稀缺的资源——时间，而且不同班组之间还会给出不一致的分类。C 作为一个动作并没有错、实践中也常常这样做，但它只解决了一名伤员，其余所有人的状态仍无记录，这与“全场景的连续性”恰恰相反。

questions.questionEn: Which statement best describes the goal of implementing culturally safe practices in paramedicine?
questions.questionZh: 下列哪一项最准确地描述了在院前急救中推行文化安全（cultural safety）实践的目标？

options.en: Ensuring all patients are treated with the same clinical protocol regardless of background
options.zh: 确保所有患者不论背景都按同一套临床方案处置

options.en: Requiring a translator for every patient who speaks a language other than English
options.zh: 凡是不说英语的患者一律要求配备翻译

options.en: Eliminating the need for subjective assessments in diverse populations
options.zh: 在多元人群中取消主观性评估的必要

options.en: Recognizing the impact of power imbalances and personal biases on patient care
options.zh: 认识到权力不平等和个人偏见对患者照护的影响

questions.explanationEn: Cultural safety differs from cultural awareness or sensitivity because it turns the examination back on the provider and the system: it asks how the uniform, the authority to decide, and the provider's own assumptions shape what the patient feels able to say and refuse. That is why the framework pairs it with a duty of self-awareness about personal and cognitive bias. A is wrong because it describes identical treatment, which is the opposite of equitable treatment - the same protocol applied without regard to context can reproduce exactly the disparities being addressed. B is wrong because interpretation is one useful tool for one specific barrier, not the goal, and mandating it for everyone ignores patient preference. C is wrong because subjective assessment - what the patient reports, values and fears - is indispensable clinical data; culturally safe practice makes those accounts more accessible rather than seeking to remove them.
questions.explanationZh: 文化安全不同于“文化意识”或“文化敏感性”，因为它把审视的方向掉转回医疗人员和体制本身：它追问的是制服、决定权，以及医护自身的预设，如何塑造了患者觉得自己“能说什么、能拒绝什么”。正因如此，能力框架才把它与“对个人偏见和认知偏见保持自我觉察”的义务绑在一起。A 错误，它描述的是“一模一样的对待”，而这恰恰是公平对待的反面——不顾情境地套用同一套方案，会原样复制它本想消除的那些差距。B 错误，翻译只是针对某一种具体障碍的有用工具，不是目标本身，一刀切地强制使用还忽略了患者意愿。C 错误，主观性评估——患者报告的感受、看重的东西、害怕的事——是不可或缺的临床数据；文化安全实践是让这些叙述更容易被说出来，而不是要把它们剔除。

questions.questionEn: An 82-year-old patient with known early-stage dementia wishes to refuse transport to hospital despite showing signs of a stroke. The patient is oriented to person and place but cannot recall the current year. Which factor is most critical in determining this patient's capacity to refuse care at this moment?
questions.questionZh: 一名 82 岁、已知患有早期痴呆的患者出现卒中征象，但希望拒绝转运至医院。该患者对人物和地点定向正常，但说不出现在是哪一年。在判断该患者此刻拒绝治疗的决策能力时，哪一项因素最为关键？

options.en: The patient's ability to understand the risks of refusing the intervention
options.zh: 患者是否能理解拒绝该干预所带来的风险

options.en: The patient's ability to recall the current date and time
options.zh: 患者是否能说出当前的日期和时间

options.en: The presence of a legally appointed substitute decision-maker
options.zh: 是否存在依法指定的替代决策者

options.en: The patient's documented history of dementia
options.zh: 病历中记载的痴呆病史

questions.explanationEn: Capacity is decision-specific and time-specific: the question is never whether this person is globally competent, but whether right now they can take in the relevant information, appreciate how it applies to them, weigh the alternatives and communicate a choice. For a refusal, the operative test is whether they understand what may happen if they do not go - in this case that an untreated stroke may cause permanent disability or death. B is wrong because orientation to time is a screening item, not a capacity test; plenty of people who cannot name the year can still reason clearly about a specific decision, and plenty who can name it cannot. C is wrong because a substitute decision-maker's authority only activates once incapacity has been established, so invoking one first reverses the order of the assessment. D is wrong and is the central trap of the question: a diagnosis never determines capacity, since early dementia is entirely compatible with retained decision-making for a specific, explained choice.
questions.explanationZh: 决策能力是“针对具体决定、在具体时点”评估的：问题从来不是这个人是否总体上有行为能力，而是他此刻能否接收相关信息、理解它对自己意味着什么、权衡各种选项，并表达出一个选择。对于“拒绝”来说，真正的检验标准是他是否明白不去会发生什么——在本例中就是未经治疗的卒中可能导致永久残疾或死亡。B 错误，时间定向只是筛查项目而不是能力测试；很多说不出年份的人仍能对某个具体决定作出清晰推理，而很多说得出年份的人却不能。C 错误，替代决策者的权限要在“已确认丧失决策能力”之后才启动，先搬出替代决策者等于把评估顺序颠倒了。D 错误，而且正是本题的核心陷阱：诊断从不决定决策能力，早期痴呆完全可以与“对一项经过解释的具体选择保有决策能力”并存。

questions.questionEn: A paramedic is called to a home where a mother is caring for her two-week-old infant. The mother appears dishevelled, speaks in a monotone, and says she 'cannot bond' with the baby. The infant appears healthy and well fed. Which interpretation of this situation is most appropriate?
questions.questionZh: 一名急救员出勤到一户人家，一位母亲正在照顾她两周大的婴儿。这位母亲衣着不整、说话语调平板，并表示自己“无法和孩子建立感情联结”。婴儿看起来健康、喂养良好。对这一情况最恰当的解读是什么？

options.en: The mother is experiencing normal fatigue associated with new parenthood
options.zh: 这位母亲只是初为人母的正常疲劳

options.en: The mother is intentionally neglecting the infant's emotional needs
options.zh: 这位母亲在有意忽视婴儿的情感需求

options.en: The mother may be experiencing postpartum depression
options.zh: 这位母亲可能正在经历产后抑郁（postpartum depression）

options.en: The mother lacks the basic skills required for neonatal care
options.zh: 这位母亲缺乏照顾新生儿所需的基本技能

questions.explanationEn: Flat affect, self-neglect and an explicitly stated failure to bond, two weeks after delivery, are the recognisable features of postpartum depression rather than of ordinary new-parent exhaustion. The paramedic's job here is not to diagnose but to recognise a treatable and potentially dangerous condition, ask directly and non-judgementally about mood and about thoughts of harm to herself or the baby, and make sure this reaches a clinician who can follow it up. A is wrong because normal fatigue does not flatten affect or abolish bonding; that framing is the reason postpartum depression is so often missed. B is wrong because the infant is well fed and cared for, so there is no evidence of intent to neglect - and reading illness as bad parenting is precisely what stops mothers from disclosing. D is wrong for the same reason: the baby's condition demonstrates that practical skills are intact, which points to a mood disorder rather than a knowledge gap.
questions.explanationZh: 产后两周出现情感平淡、自我照顾能力下降，并且明确说出“无法与孩子建立联结”，这是产后抑郁（postpartum depression）的可辨识特征，而不是普通的初为人母的疲惫。急救员在这里的任务不是下诊断，而是识别出一种可治疗、也可能危险的状况，直接而不带评判地询问她的情绪，以及有没有伤害自己或婴儿的想法，并确保这一信息传递给能够跟进的临床人员。A 错误，正常疲劳不会让情感变得平淡、也不会让母婴联结消失；正是这种“想当然”的解释使产后抑郁如此频繁地被漏诊。B 错误，婴儿吃得好、照顾得好，没有任何证据显示存在故意忽视——而把疾病读成“不称职的母亲”，恰恰是让母亲们闭口不谈的原因。D 同理错误：婴儿的状态本身就证明她的实操技能完好，这指向的是情绪障碍而不是知识欠缺。

questions.questionEn: While treating a long-time friend in a professional capacity, a paramedic is asked by the friend's family to share specific details of the friend's mental health history. Which response best maintains professional boundaries and privacy standards?
questions.questionZh: 一名急救员正以专业身份救治一位多年好友，好友的家属要求他透露该好友精神健康病史的具体细节。哪一种回应最能同时守住专业边界和隐私标准？

options.en: Discussing the details only after obtaining explicit consent from the friend
options.zh: 只有在取得该好友明确同意之后才讨论这些细节

options.en: Sharing the information immediately so the family can provide support
options.zh: 立即告知，以便家属能够提供支持

options.en: Referring the family to the friend's primary care physician for all information
options.zh: 把家属统一转介给该好友的家庭医生去了解全部信息

options.en: Declining to answer until the friend is transported to hospital
options.zh: 在把好友送到医院之前拒绝回答

questions.explanationEn: Personal health information belongs to the patient, and a capable patient decides who may receive it - being family does not create a right of access, and mental health history is among the most sensitive categories there is. Consent must also come from the patient rather than be assumed from the pre-existing friendship, which in this scenario is precisely the pressure that makes disclosure tempting. B is wrong because good intentions do not create lawful authority to disclose, and an unauthorised disclosure of psychiatric history can cause lasting harm to a relationship the patient may have deliberately kept private. C is wrong because redirecting the request does not answer it: the family physician is under the same consent obligation, so the referral merely passes along a request that still requires the patient's permission. D is wrong because arrival at hospital changes nothing about who owns the information; it defers the question rather than resolving it, and implies the information will become shareable once someone else is in charge.
questions.explanationZh: 个人健康信息属于患者本人，有决策能力的患者自己决定谁可以获知——“是家属”并不自动产生知情权，而精神健康病史更属于最敏感的信息类别之一。同意必须来自患者本人，不能因为双方原本是朋友就默认取得，而在本情境中，恰恰是这层旧交情构成了让人想开口的压力。B 错误，善意不等于合法的披露授权，未经许可透露精神科病史可能对患者刻意保护的关系造成长期伤害。C 错误，把请求转个方向并不等于回答了它：家庭医生受同样的同意义务约束，这样做只是把一个仍然需要患者许可的请求转手出去。D 错误，送达医院并不改变这份信息归谁所有；它只是把问题推后而没有解决，还暗示“换个人负责之后信息就可以说了”。

questions.questionEn: When operating in a community setting, which factor primarily determines whether a paramedic may perform a specific clinical intervention?
questions.questionZh: 在社区环境中执业时，主要由哪一项因素决定急救员是否可以实施某项具体的临床干预？

options.en: The patient's preference for a particular treatment
options.zh: 患者对某种治疗方式的偏好

options.en: The availability of the necessary equipment on the ambulance
options.zh: 救护车上是否配备了所需器材

options.en: The time elapsed since the paramedic's last training update
options.zh: 距离该急救员上一次培训更新过去了多久

options.en: The scope of practice defined by the provincial or territorial regulatory authority
options.zh: 省或地区监管机构所界定的执业范围

questions.explanationEn: Authority to perform an intervention is granted by the regulator through the licensed scope of practice for a designation; everything else operates inside that boundary. If an act is outside scope, no amount of equipment, patient request or personal skill makes it lawful. A is wrong because patients may consent to or refuse what is offered, but cannot authorise a provider to exceed their licence. B is wrong because carrying a device is a logistical precondition, not permission - the equipment being on the truck says nothing about whether this licence level may use it. C is a genuine second filter and the reason the framework pairs scope with personal competence: a paramedic must work within scope AND within their own current competence, so recency of training can restrict practice further. But it cannot expand it beyond what the regulator has authorised, which is why D is the primary determinant.
questions.explanationZh: 实施某项干预的权限，是由监管机构通过该执照等级的执业范围授予的，其他一切都在这条边界之内运作。如果某个操作超出执业范围，那么无论有多少器材、患者如何要求、个人技术多好，它都不合法。A 错误，患者可以同意或拒绝你所提供的处置，但无权授权医护超越执照行事。B 错误，车上带着某个设备只是后勤前提而不是许可——设备在车上，完全不能说明这个执照等级可以使用它。C 是一道真实存在的第二重过滤，也正是能力框架把“执业范围”和“个人胜任力”并列的原因：急救员必须同时在范围之内且在自身当下的胜任力之内，因此培训是否新近确实可能进一步限制其实践。但它无法把权限扩张到监管机构授权之外，所以 D 才是首要决定因素。

questions.questionEn: A paramedic is treating an adult patient who is unresponsive with pinpoint pupils and a respiratory rate of 6 breaths per minute. The patient's companion says the patient has been using an illicit substance. Which intervention is the priority?
questions.questionZh: 一名急救员正在处理一位无反应的成年患者，该患者瞳孔呈针尖样，呼吸频率 6 次/分。同行者称其一直在使用非法药物。哪一项干预是首要的？

options.en: Administer a carbohydrate solution orally
options.zh: 经口给予碳水化合物溶液

options.en: Perform a rapid secondary survey for trauma
options.zh: 快速进行二次检查以寻找创伤

options.en: Assist ventilation with a BVM and oxygen, then administer an opioid antagonist
options.zh: 用球囊面罩（BVM）加氧辅助通气，随后给予阿片拮抗剂

options.en: Prepare the patient for immediate intubation
options.zh: 为患者准备立即气管插管

questions.explanationEn: A rate of 6 breaths per minute is inadequate minute ventilation, and hypoxia is what kills in opioid toxicity - not the drug itself. The BC narcotic overdose guideline puts airway management and supported ventilation with oxygen to an SpO2 of at least 94% ahead of naloxone, and the naloxone dosing ladder is then titrated to that same respiratory endpoint. Ventilating first also means that if naloxone precipitates agitation or withdrawal, the patient is already oxygenated. A is wrong and dangerous: nothing goes in the mouth of an unresponsive patient, and blood glucose should be checked and corrected only if it is at or below 4 mmol/L. B is wrong because a secondary survey is a later step that does not address the immediate threat to life. D is wrong because endotracheal intubation is outside the PCP scope of practice, and it is unnecessary here since bag-valve-mask ventilation plus naloxone typically restores adequate spontaneous respiration.
questions.explanationZh: 呼吸 6 次/分意味着分钟通气量严重不足，而阿片中毒的致死机制是缺氧而不是药物本身。BC 的麻醉品过量指南把气道管理和给氧辅助通气（使 SpO2 达到 ≥94%）排在 naloxone（纳洛酮）之前，而 naloxone 的剂量阶梯随后也是按同一个呼吸终点来滴定的。先通气还有一个好处：万一 naloxone 诱发激越或戒断反应，患者此时已经处于氧合良好的状态。A 错误且危险：无反应患者口中不能放入任何东西，血糖也只有在 ≤4 mmol/L 时才需要纠正。B 错误，二次检查属于后续步骤，无法解除眼前的生命威胁。D 错误，气管插管超出 PCP 执业范围，而且在此并无必要——球囊面罩通气加 naloxone 通常就能恢复足够的自主呼吸。

questions.questionEn: You are called to a long-term care facility for an 82-year-old patient with advanced dementia who has acute agitation and is trying to leave the building. The patient is speaking incoherently and appears frightened. Nursing staff say the patient is usually calm but has become increasingly agitated over the last hour. What is the most appropriate initial clinical interpretation of this change?
questions.questionZh: 你被叫到一家长期照护机构，一名 82 岁、患有晚期痴呆的患者出现急性躁动，正试图离开该机构。患者言语不连贯、显得恐惧。护理人员表示该患者平时安静，但在过去一小时内躁动逐渐加重。对这一状态改变，最恰当的初始临床解读是什么？

options.en: The patient is likely experiencing acute delirium
options.zh: 该患者很可能正在发生急性谵妄（delirium）

options.en: The patient is experiencing a progression of their dementia
options.zh: 这是该患者痴呆病情的自然进展

options.en: The patient is having a panic attack due to environmental stress
options.zh: 这是环境压力引起的惊恐发作

options.en: The patient is exhibiting expected behavioural symptoms of aging
options.zh: 这是老化过程中可以预期的行为症状

questions.explanationEn: The decisive feature is the time course: an acute change over one hour, in a patient with a known calm baseline. Delirium is defined by acute onset and a fluctuating course, and in an older adult it is a symptom rather than a diagnosis - it means look for a cause. The differential a paramedic can actually work through on scene includes hypoxia, hypoglycemia, infection (urinary and respiratory are the usual culprits), pain, urinary retention, constipation, dehydration and new or changed medication, so vital signs, SpO2, temperature and blood glucose come next. B is wrong because dementia progresses over months to years, not over an hour; attributing an abrupt change to the underlying diagnosis is the single most common reason a treatable cause is missed in this population. C is wrong because panic attacks are uncommon as a new presentation in advanced dementia and do not explain a sustained, escalating change in behaviour. D is wrong because there is no behavioural change that is simply 'expected with age' - normal aging does not cause acute agitation, and accepting that framing forecloses the workup.
questions.explanationZh: 决定性线索是时间进程：在一个基线安静的患者身上，一小时内出现急性改变。谵妄（delirium）的定义就是急性起病、病程波动，而在老年人身上它是一个症状而不是诊断——它的含义是“去找病因”。急救员在现场真正能够排查的鉴别诊断包括缺氧、低血糖、感染（泌尿道和呼吸道最常见）、疼痛、尿潴留、便秘、脱水，以及新加或调整过的药物，因此接下来就该测生命体征、SpO2、体温和血糖。B 错误，痴呆的进展以月甚至年计，而不是一小时；把突发的改变归因于原有诊断，正是这一人群中可治疗病因被漏掉的头号原因。C 错误，惊恐发作在晚期痴呆患者中作为新发表现并不常见，也解释不了持续且逐步加重的行为改变。D 错误，根本不存在“年纪大了本来就会这样”的行为改变——正常老化不会引起急性躁动，而接受这种说法就等于直接放弃了后续排查。

questions.questionEn: A 14-year-old patient requires an emergency intervention for a severe allergic reaction. The patient is alert and oriented but refuses the intervention, saying they do not believe it is necessary. The parent, who is present, insists that it be performed immediately. Which action should the paramedic take?
questions.questionZh: 一名 14 岁患者因严重过敏反应需要接受紧急干预。该患者意识清醒、定向正常，但拒绝该干预，称自己认为没有必要。在场的家长则坚持要求立即实施。急救员应当采取哪一项行动？

options.en: Administer the intervention based on the parent's consent
options.zh: 依据家长的同意实施该干预

options.en: Assess the patient's capacity to make their own medical decision
options.zh: 评估该患者自行做出这一医疗决定的能力

options.en: Wait for the patient to change their mind before proceeding
options.zh: 等患者自己改变主意后再实施

options.en: Contact the patient's primary physician for a decision
options.zh: 联系患者的家庭医生，由其决定

questions.explanationEn: In Canada, consent for a minor turns on capacity rather than on a fixed age. A mature minor who can understand the nature of the proposed treatment, its risks and benefits and the consequences of refusing may consent to or refuse that treatment on their own, and where the minor has capacity the parent's wish does not override it. So the first act is to assess: can this 14-year-old explain what is being proposed, what happens if it is not done, and why they are declining? A is wrong because it acts on parental consent without first establishing whether it is legally operative here. C is wrong and unsafe because a severe allergic reaction can deteriorate within minutes; waiting is not a neutral option, and if the patient is found to lack capacity the intervention must proceed. D is wrong because a primary physician is not reachable in a useful timeframe and has no authority to resolve a capacity question at the bedside. Note that if the reaction progresses to anaphylaxis with decreased level of consciousness, capacity is lost and treatment proceeds under the emergency doctrine.
questions.explanationZh: 在加拿大，未成年人的同意取决于决策能力而不是某个固定年龄。所谓“成熟未成年人”，只要能理解拟行治疗的性质、风险与获益以及拒绝的后果，就可以自行同意或拒绝该治疗；在未成年人具备决策能力的情况下，家长的意愿并不能推翻它。因此第一步是评估：这名 14 岁患者能否说清楚你打算做什么、不做会怎样、以及自己为什么拒绝？A 错误，它在尚未确认家长同意在此是否具有法律效力之前就直接照办。C 错误且不安全，严重过敏反应可在几分钟内恶化，“等一等”并不是一个中性选项；而且一旦判定患者不具备决策能力，就必须立即实施干预。D 错误，家庭医生在有用的时间窗内根本联系不上，也无权在现场裁定决策能力问题。需要注意的是，若反应进展为 anaphylaxis（过敏性休克）并出现意识水平下降，患者即丧失决策能力，此时按紧急情况原则直接施救。

questions.questionEn: A 78-year-old patient with a history of hypertension is being transported after a fall at home, and says they are afraid of falling again once they return. Which of the following is the most important factor in preventing future falls in this patient population?
questions.questionZh: 一名 78 岁、既往有高血压的患者在家中跌倒后正被转运，患者表示害怕回家后再次跌倒。对这一人群而言，预防再次跌倒最重要的因素是下列哪一项？

options.en: Increasing the patient's daily intake of calcium and vitamin D
options.zh: 增加患者每日钙和维生素 D 的摄入量

options.en: Conducting a comprehensive home safety assessment
options.zh: 进行一次全面的居家安全评估

options.en: Limiting the patient's physical activity to reduce risk
options.zh: 限制患者的体力活动以降低风险

options.en: Ensuring the patient wears a medical alert bracelet
options.zh: 确保患者佩戴医疗警示手环

questions.explanationEn: Most falls in older adults happen at home and result from modifiable environmental and personal factors: loose rugs and cords, poor lighting on the route to the bathroom, absent grab bars and handrails, unsuitable footwear, clutter on stairs, and medications that cause postural hypotension. A structured home assessment is the intervention that finds and fixes those, and paramedics who see the home are uniquely placed to flag them for referral. A is wrong because calcium and vitamin D address bone density, which affects whether a fall causes a fracture, not whether the fall happens. C is wrong and counterproductive: restricting activity accelerates the loss of strength and balance and therefore raises fall risk, whereas strength and balance exercise lowers it. D is wrong because an alert bracelet shortens the time spent on the floor after a fall - valuable, but a response measure rather than prevention.
questions.explanationZh: 老年人的跌倒多数发生在家里，源于可改变的环境和个人因素：松动的地毯与电线、通往卫生间路线上照明不足、缺少扶手和抓杆、不合适的鞋、楼梯上的杂物，以及会引起体位性低血压的药物。结构化的居家安全评估正是能把这些找出来并加以整改的干预，而进过患者家门的急救员，恰恰最有条件把这些问题记录下来并转介出去。A 错误，钙和维生素 D 针对的是骨密度，它影响的是“跌倒后会不会骨折”，而不是“会不会跌倒”。C 错误且适得其反：限制活动会加速肌力和平衡能力的丧失，反而抬高跌倒风险，而力量与平衡训练才是降低风险的做法。D 错误，警示手环缩短的是跌倒后躺在地上无人发现的时间——有价值，但属于事后响应而不是预防。

questions.questionEn: A paramedic is preparing for a transfer. The oxygen cylinder reads 1,200 psi, the cylinder constant is 0.28, and the flow rate is 4 L/min. Ignoring a safety reserve, how many minutes of oxygen remain?
questions.questionZh: 一名急救员正在准备一次转运。氧气瓶压力表读数为 1,200 psi，瓶系数为 0.28，流量为 4 L/min。在不计安全余量的情况下，还剩多少分钟的氧气？

options.en: 42 minutes
options.zh: 42 分钟

options.en: 65 minutes
options.zh: 65 分钟

options.en: 84 minutes
options.zh: 84 分钟

options.en: 110 minutes
options.zh: 110 分钟

questions.explanationEn: Duration in minutes equals gauge pressure multiplied by the cylinder constant, divided by the flow rate: (1,200 x 0.28) / 4 = 336 / 4 = 84 minutes. A is what you get by dividing by 8 L/min instead of 4, the commonest error being to use the flow rate you wish you were running rather than the one set. D is roughly the result of dividing by 3 L/min. B does not follow from any correct substitution. In practice this figure is an upper bound and must not be used as a transport plan: subtract a residual safety pressure - commonly around 200 psi - before calculating, because a cylinder is considered empty well before the gauge reaches zero, and remember that the number assumes the flow rate stays constant for the whole trip.
questions.explanationZh: 可用时长（分钟）= 压力表读数 × 瓶系数 ÷ 流量，即 (1,200 × 0.28) ÷ 4 = 336 ÷ 4 = 84 分钟。A 是把除数错用成 8 L/min 的结果——最常见的错误就是拿“心里想用的流量”而不是“实际设定的流量”去算。D 大致相当于按 3 L/min 计算。B 则不对应任何一种正确代入。实际操作中这个数字只是上限，不能直接拿来做转运计划：计算前应先扣掉残余安全压力（常取 200 psi 左右），因为气瓶在压力表远未归零时就已被视为用尽；同时要记住，这个结果的前提是整段转运中流量保持不变。

questions.questionEn: A paramedic is treating an elderly patient with advanced dementia. The patient's daughter, who is the legal substitute decision-maker, is present and asks the paramedic to perform a specific procedure that the patient is physically resisting. What is the most appropriate next step?
questions.questionZh: 一名急救员正在救治一位患有晚期痴呆的老年患者。患者的女儿是其法定替代决策者，她在场并要求急救员实施某项具体操作，而患者正在用身体动作抗拒。下一步最恰当的做法是什么？

options.en: Perform the procedure immediately, since the daughter has legal authority
options.zh: 既然女儿具有法律权限，就立即实施该操作

options.en: Attempt to calm the patient and explain the procedure to obtain their cooperation
options.zh: 先设法安抚患者并向其解释该操作，争取其配合

options.en: Decline the procedure until a physician can be contacted for further orders
options.zh: 在联系到医生取得进一步医嘱之前不予实施

options.en: Ask the daughter to physically restrain the patient while the procedure is performed
options.zh: 请女儿在操作过程中按住患者

questions.explanationEn: Substitute consent makes a procedure lawful; it does not make forcing it appropriate. A patient who has lost decision-making capacity retains the right to have their resistance treated as meaningful communication, and physical resistance in advanced dementia usually signals fear, pain, or simply not understanding what is about to happen. Slowing down, approaching from the front, explaining in short concrete sentences, and letting the patient see and touch the equipment resolves most of these situations and is also far safer than a struggle. A is wrong because legal authority answers who may consent, not how care is delivered, and proceeding through active resistance risks injury to patient and crew. C is wrong because a physician cannot add authority that the substitute decision-maker already holds, and the delay serves nothing. D is wrong because restraint is reserved for imminent danger, is not authorised simply because a substitute decision-maker requests a procedure, and asking a family member to apply it is unsafe and inappropriate. If calm explanation fails and the procedure is genuinely time-critical, that is the point to reassess urgency and consult, not to escalate to force.
questions.explanationZh: 替代同意让一项操作在法律上成为可行，但并不意味着可以强行实施。已经丧失决策能力的患者，仍然有权让自己的抗拒被当作有意义的表达来对待；而晚期痴呆患者的身体抗拒，通常传递的是恐惧、疼痛，或者只是不明白接下来要发生什么。放慢节奏、从正面靠近、用简短具体的句子解释、让患者看到并摸一摸器材，能化解其中大部分情况，而且远比强行拉扯安全。A 错误，法律权限回答的是“谁可以同意”，而不是“该怎么实施照护”；在患者主动抗拒时硬做，患者和班组都可能受伤。C 错误，医生并不能追加一份替代决策者本已拥有的权限，这种拖延没有任何意义。D 错误，约束只保留给迫在眉睫的危险，不会因为替代决策者提出要求就自动获得授权，而让家属去按住患者既不安全也不恰当。如果平静解释确实无效、而该操作又真的时间紧迫，那时应当重新评估紧迫性并请示，而不是升级为强制。

questions.questionEn: You are the team leader during a pediatric respiratory arrest. A junior partner is struggling to maintain an effective seal with the bag-valve mask. Which action best demonstrates situational leadership to ensure patient safety?
questions.questionZh: 你是一次儿科呼吸骤停抢救中的团队负责人。一名资历较浅的搭档难以用球囊面罩维持有效的密封。哪一项做法最能体现情境领导力并保障患者安全？

options.en: Instruct the partner to continue until the airway equipment is ready
options.zh: 让该搭档继续做，直到气道器材准备好

options.en: Take over ventilation directly and assign the partner to prepare the airway adjuncts
options.zh: 直接接手通气，并把准备气道辅助器具的任务交给该搭档

options.en: Ask the partner why they are unable to maintain the seal
options.zh: 询问该搭档为什么无法维持密封

options.en: Wait for the partner to ask for assistance before intervening
options.zh: 等搭档主动求助后再介入

questions.explanationEn: Situational leadership means matching your level of direction to the urgency and to the team member's current capability. In a pediatric respiratory arrest, ventilation is the single intervention that determines the outcome, and an ineffective mask seal means the child is not being oxygenated right now. Swapping roles is decisive without being punitive: the task goes to whoever can do it, and the junior partner is immediately given useful work rather than being sidelined. A is wrong because it accepts ineffective ventilation for a period defined by equipment readiness rather than by the patient's need. C is wrong because a teaching conversation in the middle of an arrest costs oxygenated seconds; the debrief afterwards is where that question belongs. D is wrong because it makes the correction depend on a junior team member recognising and admitting their own difficulty under maximum stress, which is exactly what a leader is there to catch.
questions.explanationZh: 情境领导力的含义，是把你介入的强度与事态的紧迫性以及团队成员当下的能力相匹配。在儿科呼吸骤停中，通气是唯一决定结局的干预，而面罩密封无效就意味着这个孩子此刻没有获得氧合。互换角色既果断又不带惩罚意味：任务交给能做到的人，同时资历浅的搭档立刻拿到了有用的工作，而不是被晾在一边。A 错误，它以“器材什么时候备好”而不是“患者需要什么”为标准，容忍了一段时间的无效通气。C 错误，在抢救中间进行教学式提问要以带氧的秒数为代价；这个问题该放到事后汇报里去问。D 错误，它把纠正的时机寄托在一位资历浅的成员能在最大压力下识别并承认自己的困难上，而这恰恰是领导者本该替他兜住的事。

questions.questionEn: After a gruelling call involving a geriatric patient with complex comorbidities and a difficult family dynamic, your partner appears withdrawn and unusually silent. Which action best supports your partner's wellbeing and team cohesion?
questions.questionZh: 在一次艰难的出勤之后——患者是一位合并多种疾病的老年人，家庭关系也很棘手——你的搭档显得退缩、异常沉默。哪一项做法最能支持搭档的身心健康并维系团队凝聚？

options.en: Ask your partner how they are feeling and listen without judgment
options.zh: 问问搭档现在感觉如何，并且不带评判地倾听

options.en: Tell your partner that the call was difficult for everyone involved
options.zh: 告诉搭档这趟任务对每个人来说都不好受

options.en: Suggest that your partner take a break while you complete the chart
options.zh: 建议搭档去休息一下，由你来完成病历

options.en: Remind your partner that this is a routine part of the job
options.zh: 提醒搭档这本来就是这份工作的日常

questions.explanationEn: Supporting a colleague starts with noticing the change and then opening a door the colleague can choose to walk through. An open question followed by genuine listening lets your partner say as much or as little as they want, keeps the judgment out of it, and gives you the information you need to decide whether peer support or a formal program should be offered. B is well-meant but generalises the experience and closes the conversation - it tells your partner how to feel rather than asking. C is a kind gesture and may well follow, but handling the paperwork removes a task without addressing the distress, and it can read as being managed rather than heard. D is the most damaging because normalising the call implies the reaction is out of proportion, which is precisely the message that teaches people not to speak up next time.
questions.explanationZh: 支持同事的第一步是察觉到变化，然后打开一扇门，让对方自己决定要不要走进来。一句开放式的询问加上真正的倾听，能让搭档想说多少就说多少，把评判排除在外，同时也给了你判断依据——是提供同伴支持就够了，还是该引导他使用正式的援助渠道。B 出于好意，但把体验一般化，实际上关上了话头：它是在告诉搭档该怎么感受，而不是在询问。C 是善意的举动，往往也确实会随后发生，但替他写病历只是拿走了一项任务，并没有触及痛苦本身，而且容易让人觉得自己是被“安排”而不是被听见。D 危害最大，把这趟任务说成日常，等于暗示对方的反应过头了——而这恰恰是那种会让人下次不再开口的信息。

questions.questionEn: You disagree with a senior colleague about a patient's capacity to refuse care, and the disagreement is becoming visible to the patient. What is the most professional way to handle this conflict?
questions.questionZh: 你与一位资深同事在“患者是否有能力拒绝治疗”的判断上产生分歧，而这场争执已经开始被患者看在眼里。处理这一冲突最专业的方式是什么？

options.en: Defer to the senior colleague's opinion to avoid further conflict
options.zh: 为了避免继续争执，服从资深同事的意见

options.en: Explain your reasoning to the patient and ask them to decide
options.zh: 把你的理由讲给患者听，让患者来裁决

options.en: Request a supervisor to mediate the disagreement immediately
options.zh: 立即请主管前来调解这场分歧

options.en: Discuss the differing clinical views privately with the colleague
options.zh: 与同事私下讨论彼此不同的临床判断

questions.explanationEn: A patient watching their care team argue loses confidence in both clinicians and, in a capacity dispute specifically, is being handed the impression that the decision about their own autonomy is a contest between staff. Stepping away for a brief, direct conversation resolves the clinical question without that cost, and it does not mean dropping your position - the disagreement still has to be worked through, just not in front of the patient. A is wrong because silence is not resolution: deferring on seniority alone abandons a patient-safety concern you judged worth raising. B is wrong because it recruits the patient into a staff dispute and is incoherent in this specific case, since the patient's capacity is the very thing in question. C is not wrong in principle, and escalation is appropriate if the private discussion fails, but calling a supervisor as the first move prolongs the visible conflict and skips the step two professionals should be able to complete themselves.
questions.explanationZh: 患者眼看着照护团队当面争执，会同时失去对两位临床人员的信任；而在“决策能力”这个具体争议里，患者收到的暗示更是：关于自己自主权的判断，竟然成了工作人员之间的角力。走到一边进行一次简短直接的沟通，可以在不付出这种代价的前提下解决临床问题——这并不意味着放弃你的立场，分歧仍然必须谈清楚，只是不要当着患者的面谈。A 错误，沉默不是解决：仅仅因为对方资历更深就退让，等于放弃了一个你原本判断值得提出的患者安全问题。B 错误，它把患者拉进了工作人员的争执，而且在本例中逻辑上自相矛盾——患者是否具备决策能力，本身正是争议所在。C 在原则上没有错，若私下沟通不成，上报升级是恰当的；但把叫主管当作第一步，会让可见的冲突持续更久，也跳过了两位专业人员本应自己完成的那一步。
